content.thinking: I need to check timing phrases for CF-2, making sure wording like "a minute" or "the hour before" reads naturally without odd constructions. I'll rephrase it as something like "it caught nearly every request right away: from the minute it switched on, every evaluation logged was on."

action_items.item: Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after the flag provider recorded it switched off.
Switch monthly-spend-feature off again until the fix in PR #376 is merged.
Roll monthly-spend-feature, and flags like it, out to a small share of requests first, with an error-rate gate before the share is widened.
Require tests that cover a flag's newly enabled code path before the flag can be switched on in production.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of io-shop requests answered with a server error rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The service's own account-page error-rate warnings peaked at {Gbac1.5}.
Why did they fail? From the onset on, account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors are not in the log lines read from before the onset.

Why did that line divide by zero? Code-Fix's reading of the code says `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides this month's spend by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, there are no such purchases, so it divides by zero.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back from either search of production changes.
Any other flag change: in the window before each read, the flag provider's history showed only one change by anyone but Argus, the switch of monthly-spend-feature.

causal_chain.step: Why was that code reached? Code-Fix's reading says `render_spend_summary` reaches it only when the monthly summary is on, which is what monthly-spend-feature enables. An admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}, the moment of the onset. Before that, the service's logs show the flag evaluated as off throughout. At the onset it evaluated the flag as on for {G971b.2} of {G971b.3} evaluations, and as on throughout after that. Reverting the flag was judged refuted. However, the log lines read show the service still evaluating the flag as on, and still failing at the same line, at {T20.2}, the time the check watched. That was after the provider recorded the flag switched off at {P2.1}. So the record does not show the service measured with the flag off.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A newly switched-on feature on the shop's account page likely tried to work out a shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing by the number of items they had bought this month, and that sum cannot be done for shoppers who had bought nothing yet this month, so their pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen of the monthly-summary path for a shopper with purchases before but none this month. Code-Fix's reading adds two such cases to tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py, and both would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have failed on the division before the flag was switched on, and the fault would have been found without reaching shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: monthly-spend-feature reached every request almost at once: soon after it was switched on, every evaluation logged was on. No staged rollout and no error-rate gate on widening the flag were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Turning the flag on for a small share of requests first would have limited failures to that share, and the errors could have been caught before every shopper was exposed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: Nobody was paged: the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person could have taken the incident up when the alert fired, and acted after the flag revert was judged refuted instead of the incident waiting at escalation.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: Argus took the incident up {T2.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Investigator placed the onset at the moment monthly-spend-feature was switched on, and named the failing line from the logs.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature, a change that could be put back, {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Code-Fix proposed a draft fix, PR #376, {T39.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The flag revert was judged refuted and monthly-spend-feature was put back on. Yet the log lines read show the service still evaluating the flag as on, and still failing at the same line, at {T20.2}, the time the check watched. That was after the provider recorded the flag off at {P2.1}. The check may never have seen the service run with the flag off.

input.root_cause: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases flagged in the current month and does not handle an empty list. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}. The account page reaches this function only on the monthly-summary path that monthly-spend-feature enables, and the exception fails the whole account page request.
input.still_at_risk: monthly-spend-feature had been put back on and the division was unchanged, so the account page would likely keep failing for any shopper who has bought before but not this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
